content: Ameloblastin, also referred to as amelin, is a protein encoded by the AMBN gene in humans. It is a specific protein found within the enamel of teeth. Although proteins make up less than 5% of the total composition of enamel, ameloblastins account for approximately 5–10% of the enamel protein content. This protein is synthesized by ameloblasts, which are specialized cells involved in enamel formation, during the transition from the early secretory phase to the late maturation phase of amelogenesis. The precise role of ameloblastin is not fully understood, but it is thought to play a critical role in regulating the elongation of enamel crystals and guiding the mineralization process of enamel during tooth development. Other key proteins involved in enamel formation include amelogenins, enamelins, and tuftelins. The AMBN gene specifically encodes the non-amelogenin enamel matrix protein known as ameloblastin. This protein is believed to be essential for the formation and mineralization of the enamel matrix. The AMBN gene is located within the calcium-binding phosphoprotein gene cluster on chromosome 4. Mutations in this gene have been linked to certain dental disorders, including dentinogenesis imperfecta and autosomal dominant amelogenesis imperfecta. These mutations can disrupt the normal function of ameloblastin, leading to defects in enamel formation. Specifically, mutations in the AMBN gene are known to cause amelogenesis imperfecta, a condition characterized by abnormal enamel development.
